readings.subsection: The Thirty Sayings: Establishing Trust
readings.title: Incline Your Ear to the Foundation of Emunah
readings.subtitle: The structural necessity of internalizing truth to establish an unbreakable, functional reliance on the Creator.
readings.text: [Proverbs 22:17] Incline your ear and hear <dn>את</dn> the words of the wise, And apply your heart to my knowledge; [18] For they are pleasant If you guard them within you; Let all of them be ready on your lips. [19] That your trust might be in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>I</dn> caused you to know today, even you: [20] Have <dn>I</dn> not previously written to you Of counsels and knowledge, [21] To cause you to know The certainty of the words of truth, To return words of truth to those who send to you?

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Justice
readings.title: YeHoVaH as the Defender of the Afflicted
readings.subtitle: A warning against predatory extraction, for the Creator's justice operates on absolute equity and will execute a reciprocal penalty.
readings.text: [Proverbs 22:22] Do not rob the poor because he is poor, And oppress not the afflicted at the gate. [23] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> pleads their cause, And shall plunder those who plunder them.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Associations
readings.title: The Contagion of Wrath
readings.subtitle: The biological and spiritual danger of aligning with chaotic, destructive forces.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24] Make no friendship with one given to wrath, And do not go with a man of rage, [25] Lest you learn his ways, And find yourself ensnared.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Economics
readings.title: The Snare of Unrighteous Surety
readings.subtitle: Relinquishing control and exposing one's foundation through foolish financial guarantees.
readings.text: [Proverbs 22:26] Do not be one of those who shakes hands in a pledge, One of those who are guarantors for debts. [27] If you do not have the means to pay, Why should he take away your bed from under you?

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Inheritance
readings.title: Preserving the Structural Inheritance
readings.subtitle: The strict prohibition against altering the established borders set by ancestral authority.
readings.text: [Proverbs 22:28] Do not move <dn>את</dn> the ancient boundary Which your fathers have set.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Diligence
readings.title: The Righteous Increase of Skill
readings.subtitle: Mastering one's designated work as a reliable mechanism to stand before sovereign authority.
readings.text: [Proverbs 22:29] Do you see a man who is skilled in his work? He does stand before sovereigns, He does not stand before obscure ones.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Discernment
readings.title: The Illusion of State Delicacies
readings.subtitle: Caution and extreme restraint when interfacing with the deceptive provisions of earthly rulers.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:1] When you sit down to eat with a ruler, Look well what is before you; [2] And put a knife to your throat If you are a man given to appetite. [3] Do not desire his delicacies, For that food is deceptive.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Economics
readings.title: The Fleeting Nature of Earthly Wealth
readings.subtitle: Ceasing from human understanding to recognize the temporal, winged illusion of unauthorized riches.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:4] Do not labour to be rich. Cease from your own understanding! [5] Do you set your eyes on that which is not? For riches certainly make themselves wings; They fly away like an eagle to the heavens.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Discernment
readings.title: Rejecting the Bread of the Disharmonious
readings.subtitle: The systemic toxicity of consuming provisions from those operating with hidden, self-serving motives.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:6] Do not eat the bread of one having an evil eye, Nor desire his delicacies; [7] For as he reckons in his life, so is he. “Eat and drink!” he says to you, But his heart is not with you. [8] You vomit the piece you have eaten, And lose your sweet words.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Instruction
readings.title: The Wasted Seed of Wisdom
readings.subtitle: Recognizing when to withhold truth from those who inherently reject the Creator's operational design.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:9] Do not speak in the ears of a fool, For he treads on the wisdom of your words.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Justice
readings.title: The Vengeance of the Strong Redeemer
readings.subtitle: The terrifying certainty of YeHoVaH's retributive action against those who exploit the defenseless or move established boundaries.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:10] Do not move <dn>את</dn> the ancient boundary, And do not enter the fields of the fatherless; [11] For their Redeemer is strong; <dn>He</dn> shall plead their cause against you.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Generational Order
readings.title: The Delivery of the Soul Through Discipline
readings.subtitle: Utilizing physical correction to structurally preserve the next generation from the pit of She'ol.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:12] Bring your heart to discipline, And your ears to words of knowledge. [13] Do not withhold <dn>את</dn> discipline from a child; If you strike him with a rod, he does not die. [14] Strike him with a rod And deliver <dn>את</dn> his being from She’ol.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: The Expected Future
readings.title: Anchoring the Heart in the Fear of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: Rejecting the temporary success of the wicked for the absolute certainty of the promised prophetic inheritance.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:15] My son, if your heart shall be wise, My heart rejoices, even I, [16] And my kidneys exult When your lips speak what is straight. [17] Do not let your heart envy sinners, But be in the fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all day long; [18] For certain, there is a hereafter, And let your expectancy not be cut off.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Biological Stewardship
readings.title: The Economic Collapse of the Glutton
readings.subtitle: How surrendering to base biological impulses and systemic laziness inevitably leads to ruin and poverty.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:19] Hear, my son, and be wise, And guide your heart in the way. [20] Be not among heavy drinkers of wine Or with gluttonous eaters of meat; [21] For the drunkard and the glutton become poor, And slumber puts rags on a man.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: The Value of Truth
readings.title: The Acquisition of Unchanging Reality
readings.subtitle: Investing fully in uncompromising truth, which brings joy and establishes harmonious order within the family structure.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:22] Listen to your father who brought you forth, And do not despise your mother when she is old. [23] Buy the truth and do not sell it – Wisdom and discipline and understanding. [24] The father of the righteous greatly rejoices, And he who brings forth a wise one delights in him. [25] Let your father and your mother rejoice, And let her who bore you exult.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Relational Purity
readings.title: The Treacherous Pit of Immorality
readings.subtitle: A grave warning against the destructive, narrow well of relationships that operate entirely outside YeHoVaH's design.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:26] My son, give me your heart, And let your eyes watch my ways. [27] For a whore is a deep pit, And a strange woman is a narrow well. [28] She too lies in wait as for a prey, And increases the treacherous among men.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Chemical Deception
readings.title: The Venom of the Serpent in the Cup
readings.subtitle: The biological disintegration and spiritual manipulation caused by surrendering physical control to intoxicating substances.
readings.text: [Proverbs 23:29] Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who feels hurt without cause? Who has redness of eyes? [30] Those staying long at the wine, Those going in to search out mixed wine. [31] Do not look on the wine when it is red, When it gives its colour in the cup, As it flows smoothly; [32] In the end it bites like a snake, And stings like an adder – [33] Your eyes look on strange women, And your heart speaks perversities. [34] And you shall be as one Lying down in the midst of the sea, And as one lying at the top of the mast, saying, [35] “They struck me, I was not sick! They beat me, I did not know! When shall I wake up? Let me seek it again!”

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Construction
readings.title: Establishing the House Through Divine Intellect
readings.subtitle: The methodical application of wisdom and knowledge to structurally secure and fill one's domain with precious resources.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:1] Do not envy evil men, Nor desire to be with them; [2] For their heart plots to ravage, And their lips talk of trouble. [3] By wisdom a house is built, And by understanding it is established; [4] And by knowledge the rooms are filled With all precious and pleasant riches.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Conflict
readings.title: The Amplification of Power Through Counsel
readings.subtitle: Waging war effectively in both the physical and spiritual realms by leaning on multiple vectors of wise, opposable strategy.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:5] Mighty is the wise in strength, And a man of knowledge strengthens power; [6] For by wise guidance you wage your own battle, And delivery is by a great counsellor.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: The Mechanics of Evil
readings.title: The Abomination of the Scoffer
readings.subtitle: Understanding the systemic disharmony engineered by those who actively plot iniquity, for whom wisdom is completely unattainable.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:7] Wisdom is high for a fool; He does not open his mouth in the gate. [8] He who plots to do evil Is called a master of evil plots. [9] The purpose of folly is sin, And the scoffer is an abomination to men.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Premial Action
readings.title: The Mandate to Intervene
readings.subtitle: The absolute requirement to rescue those stumbling toward death, fully aware that YeHoVaH accurately weighs the heart and repays based on labor.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:10] If you falter in the day of distress, Your strength is small! [11] Deliver <dn>את</dn> those taken to death, And hold back those stumbling to the kill, [12] If you say, “See, we did not know this,” Would not <dn>He</dn> who weighs the hearts discern it? <dn>He</dn> who watches over your life, Would <dn>He</dn> not know it? And shall <dn>He</dn> not repay <dn>את</dn> man according to his work?

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: The Ultimate Sweetness
readings.title: The Biological and Spiritual Fuel of Wisdom
readings.subtitle: Consuming truth as a vital nutrient to guarantee one's future and an expectant, unending hope.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:13] My son, eat <dn>את</dn> honey, for it is good, And the honeycomb, sweet to your taste; [14] Know that wisdom is thus to your being; If you have found it, there is a future, And your expectancy is not cut off.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Resilience
readings.title: The Unbreakable Cycle of the Just
readings.subtitle: The dynamic mechanism wherein the righteous continually rise from temporary failure, while the wicked face terminal collapse.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:15] Do not lie in wait, O wrong one, Against the dwelling of the righteous; Do not ravage his resting place; [16] For seven times a righteous man falls and rises, But the wrong one stumbles into evil.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Perfect Harmony
readings.title: Restraining Retributive Joy
readings.subtitle: Aligning one's emotions with divine justice rather than personal vengeance, lest the Creator's wrath be diverted.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:17] Do not exult when your enemy falls, And let not your heart rejoice when he stumbles; [18] Lest <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> see and it be evil in <dn>His</dn> eyes, And <dn>He</dn> turn away <dn>His</dn> wrath from him.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Terminal States
readings.title: The Extinguished Lamp of the Wrongdoer
readings.subtitle: Recognizing the absolute lack of continuity or structural inheritance for those operating in systemic rebellion.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:19] Do not fret because of evil-doers, And do not envy the wrong; [20] For there is no future for the evil-doer; The lamp of the wrongdoers is put out.

readings.subsection: The Sayings of the Wise: Immutable Authority
readings.title: Submission to Established Order
readings.subtitle: The sudden and unpredictable ruin that befalls those who rebel against the Creator and His delegated authorities.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:21] My son, fear <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the sovereign; Do not mingle with those who change; [22] For their calamity arises suddenly, And who knows the ruin of both of them?

readings.subsection: Further Sayings of the Wise: Legal Equity
readings.title: The Requirement of Absolute Impartiality
readings.subtitle: Upholding strict restorative justice without regard to status, ensuring harmony and societal blessing.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:23] These also are for the wise: It is not good to show partiality in right-ruling. [24] He who says to the wrong, “You are righteous” – peoples curse him, Nations despise him. [25] But those who rebuke the wrong, It is pleasant, and a good blessing comes on them. [26] He who gives a right answer kisses the lips.

readings.subsection: Further Sayings of the Wise: Economic Preparation
readings.title: The Sequence of Building
readings.subtitle: Establishing a functional, producing baseline in the field before constructing one's personal dwelling.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:27] Prepare <dn>את</dn> your outside work, And make it fit for yourself in the field; Then you shall build your house.

readings.subsection: Further Sayings of the Wise: Interpersonal Justice
readings.title: The Rejection of the Retributive System
readings.subtitle: Refusing to weaponize language or enact personal, zero-sum vengeance against a neighbor.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:28] Do not witness against your neighbour without cause, And do not deceive with your lips. [29] Do not say, “Let me do to him as he did to me; I repay each according to his work.”

readings.subsection: Further Sayings of the Wise: The Entropy of Laziness
readings.title: The Biological Decay of the Slacker
readings.subtitle: A clinical observation of how withdrawing effort and surrendering to slumber invites systemic poverty and ruin.
readings.text: [Proverbs 24:30] I passed by the field of the lazy, And by the vineyard of the man lacking heart; [31] And see, it was all overgrown with thorns; Its surface was covered with nettles; And its stone wall was broken down. [32] When I saw it, I set my heart on it; I looked and received discipline: [33] A little sleep, a little slumber, A little folding of the hands to rest; [34] And your poverty shall come, a prowler, And your need like an armed man.
